meta.title: Research paper lifecycle
meta.description: The typical path of an empirical study from first idea to publication, including ethics approval and the peer-review revision loop. Durations are illustrative and vary widely by field.

summary.headline: A paper is planned before data is collected: the proposal and ethics approval come first, and peer review usually means at least one round of revision.
points: Studies involving people need ethics approval before any data is collected
Analysis follows the plan in the proposal; changes should be reported
Peer review often returns the paper for revision, sometimes more than once
Rejected papers are commonly revised and submitted to another journal

facts.Decision types: Accept, minor or major revision, reject

data.title: Research question
data.subtitle: Gap found in the literature
data.description: A literature review shows what is already known and where a useful, answerable question remains.

data.title: Proposal
data.subtitle: Methods, sample, analysis plan
data.description: Sets out hypotheses, design, sample size and the planned analysis. Some fields pre-register this plan publicly.

data.title: Ethics approval
data.subtitle: Research ethics committee
data.description: A committee checks consent, risk, data protection and fairness to participants. Data collection cannot start without approval.

data.title: Data collection
data.subtitle: Experiments, surveys, records
data.description: Collected under the approved protocol, with consent records and secure storage.

data.title: Analysis
data.subtitle: Follow the planned methods
data.description: Runs the planned analysis first; any exploratory analysis is labelled as such.

data.title: Writing
data.subtitle: Draft and co-author review
data.description: Introduction, methods, results and discussion, checked by all co-authors before submission.

data.title: Peer review
data.subtitle: Editor and expert referees
data.description: The editor sends the manuscript to independent experts and decides: accept, revise or reject.

data.title: Publication
data.subtitle: Journal article with DOI
data.description: The accepted paper is typeset, published and given a DOI. Data and code may be shared alongside it.

steps.title: Overview
steps.description: Eight stages from top to bottom. Two are external gates: ethics approval and peer review.

steps.title: Question and proposal
steps.description: The literature review defines the question; the proposal fixes methods and the analysis plan.

steps.title: Ethics approval
steps.description: Work with people or their data goes to an ethics committee. Collection starts only after approval.

steps.title: Collect and analyse
steps.description: Data is gathered under the approved protocol and analysed as planned.

steps.title: Write and submit
steps.description: The team drafts the paper and submits it to a journal.

steps.title: Revise
steps.description: Reviewers ask for changes; the authors reply point by point and resubmit.

steps.title: Publication
steps.description: Once accepted, the paper is published with a DOI.
